checks.title: Credential written into a formula, description or help text
checks.why: Anyone with Setup access, and any tool that reads metadata, can copy it. The value is blanked out in this dictionary.
checks.fix: Move it to a Named Credential or protected custom metadata, then have the key rotated. For a managed package, raise it with the vendor.

checks.title: Custom field has no description
checks.why: Nobody can tell what the field is for or whether it is safe to change or delete.
checks.fix: Add a description in Setup: what it holds, who fills it in, and which process uses it.

checks.title: Input field has no help text
checks.why: Users filling in the record get no guidance on the hover icon.
checks.fix: Add help text where the field is on a page layout users fill in.

checks.title: Custom object has no description
checks.why: The purpose of the object is undocumented.
checks.fix: Add a description to the object in Object Manager.

checks.title: Field label does not match its API name
checks.why: The label was usually changed after creation, so reports, flows and code refer to a name users no longer see.
checks.fix: Confirm the field still means what the API name says; correct the label, or note the history in the description.

checks.title: Field label only partly matches its API name
checks.why: Abbreviations or extra words make the field harder to find by API name.
checks.fix: Usually fine; align them when convenient.

checks.title: Two or more fields share the same label
checks.why: Users and report builders cannot tell the fields apart, and data ends up split between them.
checks.fix: Rename one, or retire the one that is not used.

checks.title: Field is marked old, test or do-not-use
checks.why: The name or description says it should not be used, but it still exists.
checks.fix: Check where it is used; if nothing depends on it, delete it.

checks.title: API name looks like a copy or second version
checks.why: Names like _2, _v2, _New or _Copy usually mean an older field was replaced but not removed.
checks.fix: Check whether the original is still needed.

checks.title: Retire candidate
checks.why: Past the grace period with no measurable current value: never adopted, dormant 12+ months, or a single value only.
checks.fix: Verify against reports, dashboards and integrations, then remove it from layouts and delete it. Required fields need the requirement resolved first.

checks.title: Recently stopped being populated
checks.why: Used since it was created, but no record from the last three complete months has a value.
checks.fix: Investigate — did a process, flow or integration break?

checks.title: Rarely used (under 1% of records since creation)
checks.why: Still populated now and then, but on very few records.
checks.fix: Review — consolidate with a similar field or retire.

checks.title: Formula with no usage signal
checks.why: A formula is filled on every record by definition, so only references and its values show use: this one has no references, or always returns the same value.
checks.fix: Verify it is used in reports or list views before deleting.

checks.title: Required field that is never populated
checks.why: Salesforce requires a value, yet no record has one.
checks.fix: Check how records are saved without it; resolve the requirement or the field.

checks.title: Adopted more than a year after it was created
checks.why: The field sat unused for over a year before real use began (1% of a month’s records).
checks.fix: Informational: check it was rolled out as intended.

checks.title: Custom object has no records
checks.why: An object nobody stores data in is usually unfinished or abandoned, or belongs to an unused app.
checks.fix: Confirm it is not new or awaiting a launch, then delete it or uninstall its package.

checks.title: Object is close to a Salesforce limit
checks.why: Once a limit is reached, new fields or roll-ups cannot be added to the object.
checks.fix: Retire unused fields on this object before the next build needs one.

checks.title: Formula is close to the 3,900-character limit
checks.why: Long formulas are hard to maintain and can no longer be extended.
checks.fix: Split it into helper formula fields or move the logic to a flow.

checks.title: Picklist has more than 200 active values
checks.why: Very long picklists are hard to use and report on.
checks.fix: Consider a lookup to a reference object, or deactivate stale values.

checks.title: Active workflow rule
checks.why: Salesforce has retired Workflow Rules; they no longer get fixes and should move to Flow.
checks.fix: Use Setup > Migrate to Flow, test, then deactivate the rule.

checks.title: Active Process Builder
checks.why: Process Builder is retired and is slower than a record-triggered flow.
checks.fix: Migrate to Flow, then deactivate.

checks.title: Object runs many record-triggered flows
checks.why: More than five flows on the same save makes the run order and failures hard to follow.
checks.fix: Consolidate where possible, and set Trigger Order on the ones that remain.

checks.title: Object has both Apex triggers and record-triggered flows
checks.why: Logic split between code and flows is harder to debug.
checks.fix: Document which handles what; keep new logic in one place.

checks.title: Inactive automation left behind
checks.why: Inactive flows, Process Builders, workflow rules and validation rules clutter Setup and get reactivated by mistake.
checks.fix: Delete the ones nobody plans to bring back.

checks.title: Installed package stores no data
checks.why: Every object the package adds is empty, so the app may not be in use.
checks.fix: Confirm with its owner, then uninstall it (removes its fields from layouts and reports).
